newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to resume trade in BCN on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to resume trade in BCN on Friday.

text.p: The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) said it will resume trade in Brazilian private bank BCN today.

Trade in BCN's stock, which had been suspended Thursday, will resume after the bank sent a statement to the exchange confirming it is holding talks to sell a controlling stake to Banco BBA Creditanstalt, but denying it had already sold such a stake to the bank.

In the statement, BCN said talks would last 30 to 45 days, adding that "if these negotiations lead to an agreement which would be approved by the authorities, the market will be immediately informed." For months BCN and BBA have been plagued by speculation that a merger or takeover deal would be announced any time soon.
The acquisition of BCN by BBA would put an end to BCN president Pedro Conde's troubles to find a successor to run the day-to-day operations of the bank, newspapers said.
Earlier this year BCN merged with local bank Banco Itamarati.
Before the suspension, BCN preferred stock had been traded at 10.60 reais.
